source: NCERT Class VIII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 7.

sections.heading: 1. Matter is Made of Particles
points: **Matter** = anything that has **mass and occupies space (volume)**.
All matter is made of **tiny particles** too small to see.
The particles have **space between them** and are in **constant motion**.
Evidence: dissolving sugar/salt in water, spreading of smell (**diffusion**).

points.text: Three states, differing in particle arrangement:
sub: **Solid** — particles packed **closely**, strong forces; fixed shape and volume.
**Liquid** — particles **slightly apart**, move around; fixed volume but no fixed shape (takes the container's shape).
**Gas** — particles **far apart**, move freely and fast; no fixed shape or volume; can be compressed.

sections.heading: 3. Diffusion and Change of State
points: **Diffusion** = the spreading and mixing of particles of one substance into another (fastest in **gases**, slowest in **solids**).
Heating gives particles more energy → they move apart → **change of state** (melting, evaporation).
Cooling brings particles closer → freezing, condensation.
The particle model explains **compression** (gases compress, solids barely do).

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Matter = has mass + occupies space; made of tiny moving particles with spaces between them.
Solid: closely packed (fixed shape/volume); liquid: fixed volume, no fixed shape; gas: no fixed shape/volume, compressible.
Diffusion = mixing of particles; fastest in gases, slowest in solids.
Heating → particles move apart → change of state (melt/evaporate); cooling → freeze/condense.
Gases can be compressed (large spaces between particles).

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: In a **liquid**, particles are close but can move — fixed **volume**, no fixed **shape**.
**Gases** have the **most space** between particles → easily compressed and fastest diffusion.
Change of state is due to **energy of particles**, not creation of new matter.
